note: Which is NOT literature of the Vedic tradition -> Puranas. Chapter teaches the Vedic corpus as the four Vedas plus the later Vedic texts (Upanishads); NCERT XII Theme 2 treats Puranic literature as later literature. The Puranas are not part of the corpus taught, so the 'not' answer is derivable from the chapter.

Exact hymn count of the Rigveda (official answer 1028). NCERT Class VI (fess104) says only 'more than a thousand hymns'; the exact figure 1028 does not appear in any fetched NCERT/WBBSE page usable as a chapter source, so the exact count is not taught. An exam_note in section vedic_literature discloses this to students.

'Tamaso Ma Jyotirgamaya' -> Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. Neither the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad nor this phrase appears in the fetched NCERT pages (fess106 names only the Chhandogya Upanishad); the specific source-text attribution is therefore not taught, though Upanishads generally are taught in section upanishad_thought.

Apala, Lopamudra and Gargi belonged to the Vedic period. NCERT Class VI (fess106) names Gargi and Apala among the women thinkers famous for learning who participated in debates, in the later Vedic/Upanishadic context taught here; Lopamudra is not individually named in the fetched NCERT pages, but the question's answer (Vedic period) is fully taught.

Root of 'Yoga' found in a hymn of the Rig Veda (official answer: Rig Veda). The fetched NCERT pages present Yoga only as one of the six later systems of philosophy founded by Patanjali (fess106); the specific claim that the root of Yoga occurs in a Rigvedic hymn is not in any fetched source, so it is not taught.
